CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who presents with right elbow pain that began approximately one week ago while playing lacrosse with his children. He reports the pain is sharp and radiates down the forearm. The pain is exacerbated with any movement of the elbow. Patient recalls being struck multiple times with a lacrosse stick by his son during play. He denies falling. Patient has tried ibuprofen for a few days with some improvement in pain. He reports pain is localized to the tip of the elbow.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain. Denies abdominal pain. Lungs clear. Heart regular with known systolic ejection murmur. Otherwise unremarkable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes mellitus type 2
Systolic ejection murmur (grade 2/6, previously known)

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily
Metformin 500 mg daily
Ibuprofen as needed

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient has two children, ages 13 and 10. Plays lacrosse recreationally with his children. Follows a Mediterranean diet with low salt intake. Denies smoking and alcohol use status not documented.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure 150/90 mmHg
General: No acute distress
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur noted
Right Elbow: Pain to palpation over olecranon area of posterior elbow, mild pain with flexion and extension, normal range of motion, mild swelling and bruising noted

RESULTS
X-ray of right elbow: No fracture, no bony abnormality, normal.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right elbow contusion with associated swelling and bruising from blunt trauma from lacrosse stick. Ibuprofen 800 mg twice daily prescribed for pain and swelling. Ice application three times daily for 20 minutes per session. Recommend avoiding lacrosse for the next couple of weeks to allow healing. Patient to resume activity as tolerated once pain resolves.

Hypertension: Blood pressure elevated today, likely white coat syndrome. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Patient compliant with low-sodium diet and Mediterranean diet regimen. Continue current management.

Diabetes mellitus type 2: Blood glucose readings 80-100 mg/dL when checked. Continue metformin 500 mg daily. Obtain hemoglobin A1C to assess glycemic control and determine if medication adjustment needed in the future.

Patient to follow up with nurse for prescriptions. No further questions at this time.
